title: Well-Specified and Well-Tested? Assessing SWE-bench-Style Datasets with a Self-Evolving Agent
title_zh: 规约良好且测试充分？用自进化智能体评估SWE-bench风格数据集

paragraphs.en: 提出经验引导的自进化标注助手ExLabel，用于评估SWE数据集的任务清晰度与测试覆盖率，显著优于基线。 Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on software engineering (SE) tasks, driving the need for high-quality datasets for reliable training and evaluation. SWE-bench-style datasets (SWE datasets) are widely used to evaluate LLM-based coding agents on real-world software issues, where task clarity and test coverage directly affect whether instances are solvable and verifiable. However, quality issues persist in existing SWE datasets, and manual annotation is costly and labor-intensive, motivating LLM-based annotation. Existing approaches typically rely on static, overly general rubrics, limiting their ability to handle diverse and nuanced scenarios and often yielding high false positive rates. In contrast, human annotators draw on accumulated experience to make context-aware judgments. Inspired by this, we propose ExLabel, an LLM-based, self-evolving, experience-guided assistant for task clarity and test coverage assessment in SWE datasets. ExLabel maintains an evolving experience bank that distills cross-instance knowledge into stable yet adaptive judgment criteria and reuses relevant experience to guide the assessment of new instances. For systematic evaluation, we construct SWE-TQ, a new benchmark spanning eight programming languages, by cleaning human annotations from SWE-bench and Multi-SWE-bench. Experiments with three backbone LLMs show that ExLabel achieves the best F1 across all settings, with relative improvements of 44.2%/49.9% and 24.0%/18.4% over the best baseline for task clarity and test coverage assessment on the Python/Multilingual subsets, respectively. Moreover, a coding model fine-tuned on SWE-rebench data filtered by ExLabel resolves 66.2% of issues on SWE-bench Verified, outperforming the model trained on data filtered by the best baseline by 14.5%.
paragraphs.zh: 提出经验引导的自进化标注助手ExLabel，用于评估SWE数据集的任务清晰度与测试覆盖率，显著优于基线。大语言模型（LLMs）在软件工程（SE）任务上已展现出强大性能，这推动了对高质量数据集的需求，以实现可靠的训练与评估。 SWE-bench风格的数据集（SWE数据集）被广泛用于评估基于LLM的编码智能体在真实世界软件问题上的表现，其中任务清晰度与测试覆盖率直接影响实例是否可求解与可验证。 然而，现有SWE数据集中仍存在质量问题，而人工标注成本高昂且劳动密集，这促使人们转向基于LLM的标注。 现有方法通常依赖静态且过于宽泛的评分标准，限制了其处理多样化、细致场景的能力，并常常导致较高的假阳性率。 相比之下，人类标注者会利用积累的经验做出具备上下文感知的判断。 受此启发，我们提出ExLabel，一个基于LLM、自进化、经验引导的助手，用于SWE数据集的任务清晰度与测试覆盖率评估。 ExLabel维护一个不断进化的经验库，将跨实例的知识提炼为稳定而具适应性的判断标准，并复用相关经验来指导新实例的评估。 为了进行系统性评估，我们通过清洗SWE-bench和Multi-SWE-bench的人工标注，构建了SWE-TQ，一个涵盖八种编程语言的新基准。 使用三个骨干LLM的实验表明，ExLabel在所有设置下均取得最佳F1值，在Python/多语言子集上，其任务清晰度与测试覆盖率评估相对最佳基线分别提升44.2%/49.9%和24.0%/18.4%。 此外，在经ExLabel过滤的SWE-rebench数据上微调的编码模型在SWE-bench Verified上解决了66.2%的问题，比在最佳基线过滤的数据上训练的模型高出14.5%。
